sections.h2: Which Floyd County offices handle property tax?
sections.html:
Floyd County splits the work between a Tax Commissioner and a Board of Assessors, and both are in Rome. The Tax Commissioner is in the Floyd County Historic Courthouse at 5 Government Plaza, Suite 109, Rome, GA 30161, with a mailing address of P.O. Box 26, Rome, GA 30162. Property tax calls go to (706) 291-5146 or (706) 291-5148, weekdays from 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.

The Board of Assessors values all real and personal property in the county and the City of Rome. The county notes that the Assessor's Office relocated to the former Law Enforcement Center at 5 Government Plaza, and the tax site lists (706) 291-5143 for the assessor.

Tax for the City of Rome is on the county bill. The three rate-setters are the Floyd County Board of Commissioners, the Rome City Commission and the Floyd County Board of Education.

sections.h2: What is it like to sell a house in Rome and Floyd County?
sections.html:
Rome is built among three rivers, the Etowah, the Oostanaula and the Coosa, and the city's own water documents tie them to its early trading history. Floyd County covers 509.81 square miles of land, the largest of the three counties in the Census table with Fayette and Fannin, and had 193.4 residents per square mile in 2020.

The county is a regional hub for health care. The Census Bureau lists 2022 health care and social assistance receipts of $1,653,925 thousand in Floyd, which is more than Fayette's, even though Fayette has more residents.

A house in town and a house in the unincorporated county are valued by the same assessors but may carry a different bill, since city rates apply only inside Rome. Always ask which taxing districts cover your parcel.

sections.h2: Who lives in Floyd County and what do homes cost?
sections.html:
The Census Bureau estimated 101,378 residents in July 2025, up 2.8 percent from the 2020 base of 98,589. Renters are a big share here: only 63.6 percent of homes are owner-occupied, the lowest rate among the three counties in the table.

  • Median value of an owner-occupied home, 2020 to 2024: $217,900.
  • Median gross rent: $1,014 a month.
  • Housing units in 2025: 41,737 and 36,856 households.
  • Median household income: $65,565.
  • Persons in poverty: 14.9 percent.
  • Adults 25 and older with a bachelor's degree or higher: 25.9 percent.
  • Mean commute: 23.3 minutes, the shortest of the three.
  • Building permits in 2025: 330.

With a median home value near $218,000 and a rent just over $1,000, many Floyd County sellers are landlords or heirs of small rentals, and the tax questions below apply to them as much as to owner-occupants.

sections.h2: When is Floyd County property tax due?
sections.html:
Floyd County property taxes are generally due November 15. Real and personal property bills are generally mailed by September 1, according to the Tax Commissioner's site.

  • Interest is added monthly after the due date, and a penalty of up to 20 percent may apply.
  • Mobile home bills are mailed by February 1 and are due April 1, with a 10 percent penalty and possible citation if unpaid.
  • A United States Postal Service postmark counts for mailed payments, but a metered postmark does not.
  • Bills go to the homeowner, never to the mortgage company, so forward yours to your lender if needed.
  • Taxes unpaid for more than 90 days after the due date are subject to a tax fifa recorded with the Clerk of Superior Court, which credit bureaus can see.

The Tax Commissioner's site announced that Floyd County would hold 2026 tax sales tentatively starting May 5, 2026, with listings posted on the website. That date has passed, so ask the office when the next sale schedule is published.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Floyd County assessment?
sections.html:
Write to the Floyd County Board of Assessors at 5 Government Plaza, Rome, GA 30161 within 45 days of the date of the notice. An appeal that is not received or postmarked by the stated deadline is not accepted as valid.

Floyd County appeal path (source: Floyd County Board of Assessors)
StepWhat happensTime limit
Written appealSent to the Board of Assessors with your opinion of value45 days from the notice date
Staff reviewValue is raised, lowered or left aloneIf changed, 30 days to appeal the new value
Board of EqualizationThree members appointed by the Grand Jury for three-year terms hear itAutomatic if no change is made
Superior CourtEither side can continue after the board's decisionWritten notice to the Board of Assessors

Arbitration is available instead of the Board of Equalization, at the owner's option when the appeal is filed. Grounds are taxability, uniformity, value and denial of homestead. The estimated tax on the notice cannot be the basis. Include the map reference from your notice, the filing method you choose, your estimate of value, a short reason and a daytime phone number.

sections.h2: What homestead and special programs does Floyd County offer?
sections.html:
Floyd County has local exemptions that replace the state exemption when the local amount is larger. The tax site lists regular, veterans and elderly homestead exemptions, with an extra exemption at age 62. Apply at the Tax Assessor's Office, and bring your warranty deed if you are a first-time homeowner.

Applications may be filed all year, but must be received by April 1 of the first year you want the exemption, or the benefit starts the next year. Once granted, it renews automatically unless the residence, ownership or exemption type changes.

  • A property tax deferral is open to homeowners 62 or older with gross household income of $15,000 or less. The deferred tax is repaid when ownership changes or when the total reaches 85 percent of fair market value.
  • Agricultural property can be assessed at 30 percent of fair market value, and conservation use and similar programs require a covenant of at least 10 years.
  • Standing timber is not taxed until it is sold or harvested.
  • Manufacturers may qualify for freeport exemption, with applications between January 1 and April 1.

Anyone selling land under a ten-year covenant should ask the assessors what a sale does to it before the contract is signed.

sections.h2: What should a Floyd County seller do about the tax bill?
sections.html:
Ask the Tax Commissioner for the current balance, and write the year's split into the contract. Georgia values property as of January 1 each year, and bills are generally mailed by September 1, so a spring sale can close before the year's bill exists.

Intangible tax on a long-term mortgage is collected by the Floyd County Clerk of Superior Court, not the tax office, and a copy of the warranty deed comes from the Clerk's deed room in the new courthouse at 3 Government Plaza. If you are selling a mobile home, check that the April 1 tax and decal are current.

Assessment notices are also tied to site visits. Floyd's assessors must notify owners before inspecting, under O.C.G.A. 48-5-264.1, and visits follow a sale or purchase, new construction, an active building permit, a return, an appeal or an exemption application. Staff arrive in a marked county vehicle and carry identification.

faqs.q: When are Floyd County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Generally November 15 for real estate and business personal property. Mobile homes are due April 1, and bills for real property are generally mailed by September 1.

faqs.q: How many days do I have to appeal a Floyd County valuation?
faqs.a: You have 45 days from the date of the notice of assessment, in writing, to the Board of Assessors at 5 Government Plaza, Rome. Late appeals are not accepted as valid.

faqs.q: What penalty applies to late Floyd County property tax?
faqs.a: Interest is added monthly after November 15, and a penalty of up to 20 percent may apply. Unpaid tax may also be subject to a lien and further collection action.

faqs.q: Does the City of Rome send its own property tax bill?
faqs.a: No. Taxes for the City of Rome are included on the Floyd County tax bill. The county commissioners, the Rome City Commission and the Board of Education each set their own rate.

faqs.q: Can older Floyd County homeowners postpone paying property tax?
faqs.a: Yes, in some cases. Owners 62 or older with gross household income of $15,000 or less may defer part or all of the tax on a homestead. The deferral lasts until ownership changes or the deferred tax plus interest reaches 85 percent of fair market value.
